{{nihongo|'''Nakatomi Itate Shrine'''|中臣印達神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Harima Province]].

It is an {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, classified as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}, a former prefectural shrine, and a former shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and heihaku. Because it is located in the district named Nakatomi (pronounced Nakajin),<ref>The former {{ill|Nishiharima|Q11628288|qid=Q11628288}} region’s {{ill|Issai district|Q11498436|qid=Q11498436}} Nakatomi Village ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nakajin Village}}), Nakatomi of {{ill|Ibo|Q17193534|qid=Q17193534}}, later part of {{ill|Tatsuno|Q2570410|qid=Q2570410}}</ref> it is locally called “Nakajin–Indatsu Shrine,” using the on’yomi reading. It enshrines together the Engishiki-listed '''Awaji Shrine''' through {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}}
At present, it also enshrines {{ill|Takemikazuchi|lt=Takemikazuchi|Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|lt=Ōkashima-no-Kami}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōkayama-toomi-no-Kami}}, the deities of the Engishiki Awaji Shrine.

=== History ===
It is traditionally said to have been founded on the 15th day of the 6th month of {{ill|Hōki|Q18520676|qid=Q18520676}} 1, and it is listed as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}. From the medieval period, however, due to {{ill|Ryobu Shinto|Q4402813|qid=Q4402813}}, ascetic practitioners became involved in shrine affairs and the Twelve Gongen that had been on the mountain behind the shrine were enshrined together in the main shrine. Until the early modern period, the shrine was called {{ill|Zaō Gongen|Q10514059|qid=Q10514059}}. On October 10 of Meiji 10, after a formal petition, it reverted to its original name, Nakatomi Itate Shrine. In the same month and year,<ref>Also said to be May of Meiji 12</ref> it was ranked as a prefectural shrine.

=== The Tsubuoka legend and the Engishiki Tsubuza Amaterasu Shrine ===
The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|ja|播磨国風土記|ko|하리마 국 풍토기|simple|Harima-no-Kuni Fudoki|zh|播磨國風土記|qid=Q11498726}} records that the name “Tsubuoka,” the origin of the name Ibo Village in {{ill|Ibo District, Hyōgo|Q1042150|qid=Q1042150}}, comes from the story that “when {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ashihara Shikō-no-Mikoto}} came to this mountain to dispute possession of the land with {{ill|Amenohiboko|fa|آمه‌نوهیبوکو|fr|Amenohiboko|id|Amenohiboko|ja|アメノヒボコ|ko|아메노히보코|zh|天日槍|qid=Q713100|lt=Ame-no-Hiboko-no-Mikoto}} and ate a meal, grains of rice fell.”<ref>Lines 283–288</ref> This Tsubuoka is identified with Mount Nakatomi behind Nakatomi Itate Shrine, and the Engishiki Tsubuza Amaterasu Shrine stands within the precincts.<ref>Sources such as “Jingishi-ryō,” “Harima Kagami,” “Harima Meisho Junran Zue,” and “Ibo District Gazetteer” also suggest a connection between the Engishiki Myōjin Taisha Tsubuza Amaterasu Shrine and the Tsubuoka tradition at the Hachiman Shrine located in Iseyano, Hayashida Village, Ibo District (present-day Kamiiise, Hayashida-chō, Himeji City).</ref>

=== Nakatomi Itate Shrine as a candidate for an Engishiki shrine ===
There are several theories: that this shrine located in Nakajin Village of {{ill|Ittō district|ja|揖東郡|zh|揖東郡|qid=Q11498435}} (Ibo Town Nakatomi, Tatsuno City) is the Engishiki Nakatomi Itate Shrine; that the Hachiman Shrine on Mount Matsuo in Okusami Village, Itō District (Hachiman, {{ill|Hayashida|ja|林田町|ko|하야시다정|qid=Q11533214}}, {{ill|Himeji|ar|هيميجي (هيوغو)|az|Himeci|azb|هیمه‌جی، هیوقو|be|Хімедзі|bg|Химеджи|ca|Himeji|ce|Химедзи (гӀала)|ceb|Himeji (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Himedži (Hjógo)|de|Himeji|eo|Himeĵi|es|Himeji|et|Himeji|eu|Himeji|fa|هیمه‌جی، هیوگو|fi|Himeji|fr|Himeji|ga|Himeji|gl|Himeji|he|הימג'י|hy|Հիմեձի|id|Himeji, Hyōgo|it|Himeji|ja|姫路市|jv|Himeji|ko|히메지시|lt|Himedžis|mdf|Химэдзи|mg|Himeji|mzn|هیمه‌جی، هیوگو|nl|Himeji|no|Himeji (Hyōgo)|os|Химедзи (сахар)|pl|Himeji|pt|Himeji (Hyōgo)|ro|Himeji|ru|Химедзи (город)|sco|Himeji, Hyōgo|sh|Himeji|simple|Himeji, Hyōgo|sr|Химеџи|sv|Himeji|szl|Himeji|tg|Ҳимеҷи|th|ฮิเมจิ|tl|Himeji|tr|Himeji|tt|Химедзи (шәһәр)|uk|Хімедзі|ur|ہیمیجی، ہیوگو|uz|Ximedzi|vi|Himeji, Hyōgo|war|Himeji|zh|姬路市|zh_classical|姬路市|zh_min_nan|Himezi-chhī|zh_yue|姫路|qid=Q209801}}) is the Engishiki Nakatomi Itate Shrine; and that the {{ill|Usuki Hachiman Shrine|ja|魚吹八幡神社|qid=Q11673954}} located in Miyauchi Village, Itō District (Miyauchi, {{ill|Aboshi|ja|網干区|zh|網干|qid=Q11607184}}, Himeji City) is the Engishiki Nakatomi Itate Shrine.

'''Awaji Shrine''' (あわちじんじゃ) is an {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}. It is enshrined together at Nakatomi Itate Shrine in Ibo Town, Tatsuno City, Hyōgo Prefecture. During the Edo period, it was called Awaniwa Shrine.

It is believed to have been enshrined together in the main hall of Nakatomi Itate Shrine sometime from the medieval period through the mid-Edo period, but the “Jingishi-ryō” identifies it with Yobira Shrine.
